paper_metadata.title: Quantum Computational Algorithms for Derivative Pricing and Credit Risk in a Regime Switching Economy

summary: The paper implements gate‑based quantum circuits for regime‑switching financial models including Markov‑chain state preparation, credit‑risk Value‑at‑Risk estimation, and European option pricing. Experiments run on IBM Brisbane, Kolkata, and Sherbrooke devices with small circuits (e.g., Markov chains up to T=24 steps and option pricing with 6 time steps), achieving MSE values on the order of 10⁻³–10⁻⁵ on simulators and ~10⁻³–10⁻² on hardware while relying on theoretical quadratic speedups from amplitude estimation.

experiments.description: Two-state T-period Markov chain state-preparation circuit evaluated on simulator and IBM Brisbane quantum hardware for regime-switching modeling.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Markov chain state-preparation circuit for two-state regime switching

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One qubit per time step plus an initial qubit; |0> encodes good state and |1> encodes bad state. State probabilities are loaded via RY rotations and controlled rotations.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare the Markov-chain probability distribution over all basis states; evaluate mean-squared error against the exact distribution.

problem_instance.description: Two-state observable Markov chain for regime switching economy.

dataset_specification.description: Transition probabilities estimated from NBER business cycle data for 1986-present and 1854-present; synthetic probabilities also tested.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Transition probabilities computed from peak/trough counts over expansion/recession months; steady-state initialization used.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Mean-squared error over N=64 Monte Carlo repetitions with S=1028 shots; compared against exact model probabilities.

noise_model.noise_type: readout error mitigation on hardware; simulator baseline noiseless

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Transition probabilities estimated from business-cycle data; steady-state probabilities computed classically.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Histogram-based MSE computation against exact probabilities.

speedup_claims.conditions: Markov-chain state-preparation circuit; exact transition probabilities; gate-based implementation
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports accurate state-preparation MSE but does not claim a quantum speedup for this circuit.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(T) circuit depth for T time steps; histogram size grows as 2^(T+1)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Requires large T with amplitude estimation or Monte‑Carlo replacement; current experiments only demonstrate state preparation accuracy.
limiting_factors: Circuit size grows with time horizon
NISQ noise dominates for larger T

notes: Hardware includes both ibmq qasm simulator and ibm brisbane quantum processor; simulator entry recorded as the primary non-QPU evaluation. The paper states circuit depth is T+1, but does not explicitly state total qubit count in a single sentence; inferred from the circuit description as one qubit per time step plus the initial qubit.
Authors only evaluate MSE of a Markov-chain state preparation circuit; no classical runtime comparison or advantage claim.

experiments.description: Static portfolio credit-risk circuit with and without regime switching, evaluated on simulator and IBM Kolkata quantum hardware.

algorithm.variant: Quantum risk analysis / credit-risk value-at-risk estimation with regime switching
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Classical calibration of default probabilities and sensitivities from regime-specific parameters; Markov-chain state probabilities encoded via controlled rotations.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Default events encoded in qubits via controlled Y-rotations; loss register computed with weighted sum and comparator; Markov-chain state loaded into an MC register.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the confidence level alpha for a given loss threshold L in a credit portfolio; equivalently compute VaR via quantum amplitude estimation.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparator flips objective qubit when total loss exceeds threshold; binary search used classically to find L for a target alpha.

problem_instance.description: Static homogeneous credit portfolio with one group of obligors, evaluated both without regime switching and with two-state regime switching.

dataset_specification.description: 1986-present transition probabilities and synthetic transition probabilities; portfolio parameters listed in Table 2.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Default probabilities and sensitivities set by regime; latent factor discretized with 2^nZ-1 values and affine mapping.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: MSE reported for simulator and quantum processor runs; exact alpha computed classically for comparison.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical computation of regime-dependent default probabilities, sensitivities, and discretized latent-factor mapping.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: MSE against exact alpha; binary search over loss threshold L.

speedup_claims.conditions: Amplitude estimation for credit-risk VaR estimation; binary search over loss threshold L; gate-based implementation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states quadratic improvement in principle, but the reported experiment is an empirical MSE comparison rather than a direct runtime speedup measurement.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(log n) binary search for L given alpha; amplitude estimation subroutine provides quadratic improvement over Monte Carlo in principle
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(n) for classical Monte Carlo estimation of alpha; O(log n) binary search for threshold search

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Large‑scale amplitude estimation circuits with many Grover iterations and fault‑tolerant qubits.
limiting_factors: Quadratic speedup only (QAE vs Monte Carlo)

notes: The paper names the IBM Kolkata Falcon processor and the qasm simulator, but does not give a single total qubit count for the full credit-risk circuit. Qubit usage is distributed across MC, Z, X, S, and objective registers, so total qubits were not explicitly reported. Circuit depth is not explicitly stated for this experiment.
Paper states amplitude estimation offers quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo but only demonstrates small-scale proof-of-concept circuits.

experiments.description: European option pricing circuit with and without regime switching, evaluated on simulator and IBM Sherbrooke quantum hardware.

algorithm.variant: Quantum amplitude estimation for European call pricing with regime switching
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Classical exact pricing benchmark used for comparison; regime-dependent parameters set from Table 4.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Brownian-motion register B and price register P; QFT/iQFT used to evolve log-price distribution; payoff encoded with linear amplitude function and comparator against strike register.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate European call option price C(t,T,K,Xt,St)=E*[exp(-∫ r(Xs)ds)(ST-K)+ | Ft] via amplitude estimation.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparator and controlled rotation implement payoff thresholding; small-angle approximation used in payoff mapping.

problem_instance.description: European-style option pricing under a two-state regime-switching economy.

dataset_specification.description: 1986-present transition probabilities and synthetic transition probabilities; strike prices 0.9 to 1.1; six-month horizon.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Log-price evolution simulated in Fourier basis; payoff scaled for small-angle approximation.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: MSE against exact classical solution; S=128, B=5, N=100.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Exact classical benchmark pricing; parameterization of regime-dependent rates and volatilities.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: MSE computation over strike prices; price recovered from measurement probability via classical formula.

speedup_claims.conditions: European call pricing with regime switching; amplitude estimation; idealized setting
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper discusses quadratic improvement in principle, but the reported table is an MSE benchmark against exact classical pricing, not a direct speedup measurement.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Amplitude estimation gives quadratic improvement over Monte Carlo in principle; paper notes ideal error scaling O(M^-2/3) for the pricing setup with scaling constant c, versus O(M^-1) for credit-risk example in their discussion
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Monte Carlo pricing error scales as O(M^-1/2)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Fault‑tolerant amplitude estimation with many oracle calls and deeper payoff circuits.
limiting_factors: Only quadratic speedup from amplitude estimation
Scaling constant c introduces sampling error tradeoff
Circuit depth large due to QFT and arithmetic

notes: The paper reports the hardware and evaluation settings but not a single explicit total qubit count or total circuit depth for the full pricing circuit. The circuit uses registers B, P, Str, Obj, and MC, so total qubits are not directly stated.
Authors explicitly discuss theoretical quadratic speedup vs classical Monte Carlo but note NISQ limitations.

experiments.description: Practical dynamic portfolio credit-risk / VaR estimation using iterative amplitude estimation on a regime-switching Aaa/Baa bond portfolio, evaluated on IBM qasm simulator.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) for dynamic portfolio VaR
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Classical Markowitz mean-variance solution used to derive regime-dependent portfolio weights and growth mapping.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Growth register G encoded in binary with sign qubit; Markov chain controls additions of relative growth rg over time; objective is probability that G < 0.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate alpha = P(G < 0) for a loss threshold L' in a dynamic portfolio under regime switching.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Classical mapping L' = L - Lmax to reduce qubit count; sign qubit serves as objective bit.

problem_instance.description: Dynamic portfolio of Aaa and Baa bonds with regime-dependent mean-variance weights and Markov switching between good and bad economies.
problem_instance.dataset_name: NBER business cycle chronology; Aaa/Baa bond series

dataset_specification.description: Monthly Aaa and Baa series from 1986 to end of 2022; regime statistics computed from NBER expansions and recessions.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute regime-specific means, standard deviations, and correlations for Aaa/Baa returns; derive Markowitz weights; map worst-case loss Lmax and relative growth rg.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Iterative amplitude estimation with 100 shots per iteration; compare estimated alpha and confidence interval to ideal alpha; report ideal complexity and transpilation overhead.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical Markowitz optimization and regime-statistics estimation from bond data.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert measured probability to alpha; compare to ideal alpha and confidence interval.

speedup_claims.conditions: Iterative amplitude estimation for dynamic portfolio VaR; 95% confidence interval; epsilon = 0.1; k = 1; 100 shots per iteration
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports estimated alpha, confidence intervals, and ideal two-qubit-gate complexity, but not a measured runtime speedup over classical Monte Carlo.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: IQAE provides quadratic improvement over classical Monte Carlo; paper reports ideal complexity values 1082 and 12932 two-qubit gates for 3 and 6 time steps respectively
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical Monte Carlo error scales as O(M^-1/2)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Large fault‑tolerant systems capable of running full amplitude estimation with deep Grover operators.
limiting_factors: Connectivity overhead roughly doubles two‑qubit gates

notes: The paper reports ideal two-qubit-gate complexity and transpilation overhead, but not a total qubit count or explicit circuit depth for the full dynamic-portfolio circuit.
Section 5 discusses theoretical scaling advantage of amplitude estimation but notes canonical QAE circuit is infeasible to transpile for current hardware.

experiments.description: Dynamic portfolio credit‑risk Value-at-Risk estimation using Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) for a regime-switching bond portfolio model.
key_results: IQAE estimates of α ≈ 0.05 confidence-level loss probabilities for dynamic portfolios
For 3 time steps: ideal α = 6.4%, estimate = 7.7%, CI ≈ 2.2%
For 6 time steps: ideal α = 4.5%, estimate = 6.0%, CI ≈ 1.9%
Ideal circuit complexity: 1082 and 12932 two‑qubit gates respectively
Connectivity overhead on IBM Sherbrooke-like hardware ≈ 2×
